notes.text:
Retain k algebraically closed, characteristic zero and trivially valued; X smooth integral projective of dimension n>=1; L any actual big rational bundle; theta=c1(L), K=X^an, v0 the generic trivial valuation and V=vol(L)>0. There is no countability, toric, skeletal, support or finite-generation restriction. The only caller grants used are G0 in its actual ample domain and G1 in its exact resolved relative-generation and single-FS-net signature. Ordinary background is characteristic-zero model resolution, actual Kodaira decomposition, openness and eventual generation of ample bundles, normal proper birational section descent, rational model density, section-volume asymptotics and ordinary algebraic volume-root concavity.

Define PSH(theta) by one all-point decreasing net of full, possibly polar FS scalars on actual B_i with c1(B_i)->theta and finite generic endpoint. A generated zero-weight system has scalar zero at every semivaluation: a generator is a unit at its center. Tensoring therefore preserves the scalar. If Omega-L is ample, an incoming tail embeds into actual Omega; appending floors max(h_i,-N) gives one finite-valued defining product net. G0 then supplies finite divisorial values and all-point order determination. Scalar suprema equal generic values. Maxima have single defining nets by tensoring into valid common L+epsilon A targets. Real convexity follows from r_j(h_i-C)+s_j(g_l-C)+C, with positive rational coefficients increasing to r and 1-r and stages below C. Integer scaling uses tensor powers. None of these operations assumes twice-decreasing closure.

Fix the actual Kodaira identity L=aA+E0, with a>0 rational, A ample and E0 effective. Write W=q_E0<=0 and Z=E0^an. W is finite continuous off Z and is a section scalar on L-aA. For bounded continuous f and genuine u<=f, take its defining h_i on M_i. Fix rational 0<t<1 and epsilon>0 before choosing a tail. The actual bundle C_i,t=L-(1-t)M_i-t(L-aA) tends numerically to taA, so is ample on a tail. The compact closed sets {h_i>=f+epsilon} decrease to the empty set; hence h_i<f+epsilon everywhere eventually. Tensor actual sections with a generated zero system on C_i,t. The resulting actual L scalar F=(1-t)h_i+tW-epsilon-t||f|| satisfies F-f<=-t f+tW-t||f||-t epsilon<=0, including supported poles. At x outside Z, first take the defining tail, then epsilon to zero, then rational t to zero. Thus the full actual L-section supremum Q_L(f) is at least u(x). Conversely section minorants are genuine, so Q_L(f)=P_theta(f) off Z even before genuine envelope existence is assumed.

For rational model f, G1 supplies one genuine endpoint psi with Q_L(f)<=psi<=f. The preceding argument makes every competitor <=psi at divisorial valuations. Common actual ample embedding and G0 determine the all-point order. Consequently psi=P_theta(f) genuinely. In particular R=P_theta(0) is genuine, R(v0)=0, and dominates all normalized genuine functions. For each big actual B, a normalized late G1 reference stage psi_B obeys R_B<=psi_B+c_B for its finite generic shift. Normalization of these stages is not asserted to preserve monotonicity.

The closure argument uses an extra old-pole bound. If F is FS, F>=(1-delta)psi-k, psi<=0 FS, and h<=psi+C is usc, then h-F on the finite locus, assigned -infinity at poles of F, is usc because h-F<=delta psi+C+k near those poles. This assigned comparison extension is not subtraction of infinities. Compact nested superlevels give a uniform negative tail.

For u_i decreasing to u with finite generic value, restrict to u_i<=M. A special stage on T_eta=L+eta A has F>=u+kappa and F>=(1-delta)psi-k, where psi is a normalized late G1 stage for B=L+epsilon A, epsilon<eta/4. Its actual bundle is close enough to tensor the weakened floor into T_eta. Every late defining stage h of a fixed u_i, embedded in an old B_l, satisfies h<=R_B_l+M+1<=psi_l+c_l+M+1. Given finitely many old special stages, choose new eta below their epsilon_l, and a new reference whose bundle embeds in every B_l. Then psi<=R_B_l<=psi_l+c_l. Choose delta below every old delta_l. A large k makes the new floor b=(1-delta)psi-k lie below all old F_l, since b-F_l<=(delta_l-delta)psi_l+(1-delta)c_l+k_l-k; it is -infinity at old poles. Choose kappa below one quarter of every old guard. Apply the comparison lemma first to u_i+2kappa and then to a defining tail of that fixed u_i. This produces h+kappa<=F_l simultaneously. The new max(h+kappa,b) is a special stage below all old stages. These stages form a directed decreasing net with eta tending to zero. At any x and finite t>u(x), a late u_i and defining h, a small guard and a low floor give a stage below t at x. Their single all-point infimum is therefore u, including -infinity. This proves genuine decreasing closure through actual reference control, rather than abstract flattening.

Directed rational model majorants and this closure give genuine envelopes for upper bounded usc obstacles having a genuine minorant. For bounded continuous f, P_theta(f)=Q_L(f) off Z. The section supremum is lsc there, the genuine envelope is usc, and both are finite. Hence every bounded continuous envelope is continuous there. G1 identifies complete relative-system suprema with Q_L(f) for model obstacles. Both discrepancies P_theta(f)-Q_L(f) and R-Q_L(0) vanish outside the same Z. This extends the zero-obstacle bridge to bounded test obstacles and matches the pinned Addendum Lemma 1.5.

Scalar energy is constructed from full section lattices. On a smooth equivariant model with central fiber F=sum b_E E and vertical D, the actual relative lattice has adapted form sum_j t^{-w_mj}k[t]s_mj, with ma<=w_mj<=mb when aF<=D<=bF. Gluing at infinity gives h0(m(rho_X^*L+D+cF))=(mc+1)h0(mL)+sum w_mj for c>-a. Actual section-volume limits give vol_Y(rho_X^*L+D+cF)=(n+1)cV+(n+1)mathscrE(f_D). Its intercept is birationally invariant, monotone, V-translation equivariant and V-Lipschitz. Volume-root concavity expanded as c tends to infinity gives concavity. Uniform model density extends mathscrE to C(K).

Equivalently, W_m(f;s)=inf_K(mf-log||s||) defines closed-endpoint linear upper-weight spaces and an adapted finite flag. The full trace is lim n!m^{-n-1}sum floor(W_m(f;s_mj)). Model weights coincide with lattice weights. The bound |e_m(f)-e_m(g)|<=(n!h0(mL)/m^n)(||f-g||+1/m) proves this continuous extension agrees with the trace.

Define E(u)=inf_{continuous f>=u}mathscrE(f) and the entire actual E1(theta)={u in PSH(theta):E(u)>-infinity}. A weighted section lies below f iff it lies below P_theta(f); their full flags agree. Every continuous majorant of P_theta(f) has at least f's weights, proving E(P_theta(f))=mathscrE(f). Thus E(R)=0 and E(u+c)=E(u)+cV, using raw volume rather than nonnef self-intersection. Compact comparison with f+epsilon proves decreasing-net energy continuity, including -infinity. Continuous concavity on product nets of majorants gives outer-energy concavity. Genuine max(u,R-N) decreases to normalized u and has energy >=-NV. This defines all actual finite-energy tests without imposing bounded relative singularities.

This is scalar theory only. Polar physical complete-system functions are not declared original E1: on P1 with O(1), the floors of log||z1|| have energy -N/2 and their pole has energy -infinity.

notes.detailedSummary: Corrected coefficients n-j give d_A(xi,eta)<=n(n+1)(e_A(xi)-e_A(eta)) for ordered bounded nef model potentials. Finite slot estimates then give a moment bound with energy gap exponent 2^{-n}. Under explicit package F, this transfers to all ordered actual E1 pairs and bounded-cost output families. notes.text:
Use n1's cone, genuine envelopes, reference R, scalar E and bounded-obstacle section result, in its entire big rational-bundle domain. All output assertions below are conditional on F; historical supplied bodies are not grants.

Finite calculation. On one actual nef generic A, bounded relatively nef model scalars have positive raw mixed measures retaining b_E restriction coefficients and mass A^n. Put T_xi=(A,xi), e_A(xi)=T_xi^{n+1}/(n+1), J_A(xi)=xi(v0)A^n-e_A(xi), ||f||_Gamma^2=-(0,f)^2 Gamma, and d_A(xi,eta)=max_{j<n}||xi-eta||^2_{T_xi^j T_eta^{n-1-j}}. Finite vertical Hodge gives Cauchy–Schwarz. Two telescopes give, with S=(0,xi-eta), T_eta^{n+1}-T_xi^{n+1}+(n+1)S T_eta^n=-sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(n-j)S^2 T_xi^j T_eta^{n-1-j}. Each summand occurs for k=j+1,...,n. Accordingly J_A(xi)=(n+1)^{-1}sum(n-j)||xi||^2_{T_xi^j T_0^{n-1-j}}. The coefficient j+1 is false in this factor order. On the actual blowup of (p,0) in P2×P1, the relatively ample H-aE has E^3=1 and H^3=H^2E=HE^2=0. Hence J=a^3/3, the T0 seminorm is zero and the Txi seminorm is a^3; the wrong order gives 2a^3/3.

For xi>=eta, Delta=e_A(xi)-e_A(eta) equals (n+1)^{-1}sum_{k=0}^n int(xi-eta)T_xi^k T_eta^{n-k}. All summands are nonnegative, so every endpoint integral is <=(n+1)Delta. The tangent remainder -Delta+int(xi-eta)MA_A(eta) is <=n Delta. Its corrected expansion has every seminorm coefficient >=1/(n+1). Therefore d_A(xi,eta)<=n(n+1)Delta, without a volume denominator or generic normalization.

For the finite slot estimate, average slots make d_A comparable to the squared seminorm in T_(xi+xi')/2^{n-1}. The tangent remainder is comparable to d_A and convex in its first potential. Set f=xi-xi', tau=(xi+xi')/2, a=d_A(xi,xi'), b=max(d_A(xi,eta),d_A(xi',eta)), and b_j=||f||^2_{T_eta^j T_tau^{n-1-j}}. Then b0<=C_n a and b_(n-1)<=4b. Replacing a slot, splitting the second f into T_xi-T_xi', and applying Cauchy–Schwarz with T_xi,T_xi'<=2T_tau gives b_(j+1)-b_j<=C_n sqrt(b_j b). If a<=b, induction gives b_j<=C_n a^{2^{-j}}b^{1-2^{-j}}; otherwise the last-slot bound suffices. Applying this through a third potential yields d<=C_n b^{2^{1-n}}max(d,b)^{1-2^{1-n}}, hence the quasi-triangle bound. Expanding averages of nef slots gives the mixed-slot estimate with exponent 2^{1-n}. For n=1 the empty-slot seminorm supplies the argument directly.

Telescoping nth powers from j=0 and applying Cauchy–Schwarz yields, with alpha=2^{-n}, |int(xi-eta)MA_A(psi)-(xi(v0)-eta(v0))A^n| <= C_n d_A(xi,eta)^alpha J_A(psi)^{1/2}max(J_A(xi),J_A(eta),J_A(psi))^{1/2-alpha}. These are finite nef-model algebra/Hodge statements, also obtainable by fixed-model ample perturbation through G0. No ample unbounded estimate is transferred by deleting its hypothesis. When A^n=0, positive raw top measures vanish; they are not probabilities.

Exact conditional package F. F1: a target-independent M exists on every actual E1(theta), with positive original Radon mass V and constant invariance. At model envelopes it is the finite divisorial volume-derivative measure mu_D=sum_E b_E<(rho_X^*L+D+cF)^n>.E delta_vE for large c. Canonical normalized nonpositive model-envelope majorants u_i=P(f_i) decrease to every actual u, their energies decrease, and mu_D_i converges weakly to M(u). F2: actual common full-system resolutions give p_m^*L=A_m+T_m, mA_m generated, T_m effective, and phi_m,D=q_Tm+psi_m,D, phi_m,0=q_Tm, with bounded relatively nef psi on the same A_m. Pushed top products converge to mu_D, A_m^n->V, auxiliary energies converge to genuine envelope energies, and normalized generic errors tend to zero. Ordered full lattices give ordered psi. Full mixed moving products converge against each fixed signed Cartier test, whose nef decomposition is fixed before degree. F3: for nonpositive model obstacles of cost<=B, time-deficient derivative measures are positive and satisfy 0<=mu_D,c<=mu_D coefficientwise, with mass deficit <=B/c for c>B/V. Outer-envelope energy differentiates at every actual E1 base in all original continuous directions, with both signs and derivative int h dM(u). This whole package needs an independent complete audit. It contains no inverse equation or fixed-target strong integration. Moving-subspace transfers must retain (min f)(V-A_m^n) with original continuous f fixed before degree. Physical q_Tm+psi is never treated as original E1.

Under F, normalized model envelopes a>=b from ordered obstacles satisfy int(a-b)dM(w) <= C_n[E(a)-E(b)]^alpha B(w)^{1/2}max(B(a),B(b),B(w))^{1/2-alpha} at every model output w. Keep the finite generic error before the moving-degree limit. To identify the integral, squeeze each bounded relative quotient separately: fixed-degree lower bounds max(-C,phi_q,H-R) are lsc, and upper bounds min(C,P(f_H)-phi_q,0) are usc. By n1 their endpoints coincide outside Z. A continuous cutoff equal to one on the finite divisorial output support and supported where the stages are finite allows Radon-net semicontinuity to squeeze the integrals. The omitted mass tends to zero. This uses neither uniform quotient convergence nor subtraction at supported infinities.

Uniform collars require more than pointwise algebraic nullness. For actual effective S, set a_S=-log||s_S||. On a fixed determination choose ample T and d with dT-rho_X^*S nef. The pulled divisor's vertical coefficients are b_E v_E(s_S), and its horizontal remainder has nonnegative volume derivative. For gamma=rho_X^*L+cF, positive-product order paired only with fixed nef T gives int a_S dmu_D,c <= <(rho_X^*L+D+cF)^n>.rho_X^*S <= d<gamma^n>.T=:C_c,S. F3's positive tail therefore gives int min(a_S,N)dmu_D<=C_c,S+NB/c. Weak convergence of these original continuous caps passes this to M(u), B(u)<=B. Thus sup_{B(u)<=B}M(u){a_S>=N}<=C_c,S/N+B/c. Choose c first, then N. This proves algebraic nullness and uniform collars for bounded-cost output families.

Every bounded relative model test R-a is continuous off Z by n1. A continuous cutoff chi_N equal to one for a_E0<=N and zero for a_E0>=2N makes chi_N(R-a) an actual original continuous function, extended by zero near Z. The uniform collar bound gives small absolute error. Hence bounded relative integrals converge under weak bounded-cost output nets, extending the preceding gap bound to each fixed arbitrary output M(u).

Let normalized model envelopes v_i decrease to any actual normalized v in E1. Apply the gap bound to v_i>=v_j at fixed i and output, then use monotone convergence as j tends to its genuine endpoint. This gives int(v_i-v)dM(u) <= C_n[E(v_i)-E(v)]^alpha B(u)^{1/2}max(B(v),B(u))^{1/2-alpha}. Taking upper test R also gives all-test relative integrability. The approximation error tends uniformly to zero over B(u)<=B. In dimension one its expression is C_1 sqrt((E(v_i)-E(v))B(u)), including zero cases.

For fixed v and output cost bound B, choose i for a small gap error, then fix c and N for a small collar error using the fixed bound C_i=||R-v_i|| off Z. The actual continuous b=chi_N(R-v_i), extended by zero near Z, obeys sup_{B(u)<=B}int|(R-v)-b|dM(u)<epsilon, since the absolute error is bounded by v_i-v+(1-chi_N)(R-v_i). Indices and collars are fixed before the measure limit. This also gives uniform integrable tails for the fixed test: with C=||b||, (R-v)1_{R-v>2C}<=2|(R-v)-b|.

The gap extends to ordered actual tests a>=b. Choose model obstacles f_lambda decreasing to a and g_tau decreasing to b, and use ordered envelopes P(max(f_lambda,g_tau))>=P(g_tau). Their energies decrease and their separate integrals converge at a fixed finite output. This proves the same bound for actual pairs at model outputs. The fixed-test absolute approximants then identify their separate integrals along canonical output approximants of arbitrary u, giving the bound for all actual a>=b and all M(u).

For any genuine normalized u_j decreasing to u, set H_j(t)=E(P(u_j+t h)), h continuous. These are finite concave functions decreasing pointwise to H(t)=E(P(u+t h)). Their derivatives at zero are int h dM(u_j) by F3. The two secants bound that derivative between (H_j(t)-H_j(0))/t and (H_j(0)-H_j(-t))/t. Take the net limit at fixed positive t and then t to zero. Both derivative signs imply M(u_j)->M(u) weakly. For any genuine normalized v_j decreasing to v, the actual ordered gap estimate gives int(v_j-v)dM(u_j)->0. Approximate the fixed R-v by b above and multiply by any fixed continuous test. Consequently (R-v_j)M(u_j)->(R-v)M(u) weakly for these genuine decreasing nets. This does not identify all mixed-moving quotients whose physical tests need not be original E1.

Whole supporting planes follow conditionally. At a model obstacle, finite derivative and concavity give E(v)<=mathscrE(f_D)+int(v-f_D)dmu_D for every actual E1 v by continuous majorants at finite support. Applying this to a=P(f_D), whose energy is mathscrE(f_D), forces int(f_D-a)dmu_D=0. Thus E(v)<=E(a)+int(v-a)dM(a). For canonical a_i decreasing to u, fixed-test approximation identifies int(v-u)dM(a_i), and the gap estimate makes int(a_i-u)dM(a_i) vanish. Passing to the limit gives E(v)<=E(u)+int(v-u)dM(u) for all actual E1 bases/tests, restoring constants with raw mass V. Every proposed solution M(u)=nu therefore maximizes E+I_nu. Neither existence nor strict separation follows.

The proof and exact F antecedents are in paper.tex Sections 7–10. Complete pinned BJ finite Hodge/slot units are renderer 2705–2789 and 2858–3107; the coefficient identity is independently corrected. notes.text:
Use n1's full big domain, actual cone, reference R and scalar energy. For an actual effective integral Cartier divisor D, put a_D=-log||s_D||. Fix rational t>0 with L-tD big and integer N>=1. The original continuous obstacle f=-min(t a_D,N) has genuine minorant R-N and genuine envelope u. It satisfies R-N<=u<=R and u<=-N on D^an.

In every denominator-cleared admissible degree, multiplication by s_D^{mt} injects the entire H0(m(L-tD)) into H0(mL), preserving its rank. Every nonzero image vector has logarithm <=-mt a_D<=m f everywhere, and equality holds at v0. At supported zeros its logarithm is literally -infinity and remains below the finite cap. Its full-filtration weight is exactly zero. All other original section weights lie in [-mN,0], since canonical section norms are <=1 and the generic value gives the upper bound. An adapted full basis therefore has at least h0(m(L-tD)) zero weights; the other floored weights remain >=-mN. Dividing the trace by m^{n+1}/n! and using both actual section-volume limits gives 0<=B(u)<=N[V-vol(L-tD)]. The image sections themselves give actual L minorants of generic value zero, so normalization does not shift or alter the cap. n1's envelope-energy identity justifies the genuine energy calculation.

Set lambda_j=2^{-j}, N_j=4^j. For each fixed N_j, ordinary volume continuity inside the big cone permits rational t_j with L-t_jD big and N_j[V-vol(L-t_jD)]<=2^{-j}. The actual finite convex combinations w_q=sum_{j<=q}lambda_j u_j+2^{-q}R are normalized and decrease, since u_j<=R. Concavity gives E(w_q)>=-sum_{j<=q}4^{-j}>=-1/3. Genuine decreasing closure and energy continuity from n1 yield an actual original w_D in E1 with energy >=-1/3. On the whole D^an, w_q<=-sum_{j<=q}2^j, so w_D=-infinity. No abstract completion point is introduced.

Let nu be positive original Radon mass V, with nu{R=-infinity}=0, integrating R-u for every normalized actual u in E1. Apply this to w_D. Its relative gap is infinite on D^an outside the reference poles, so those points have zero mass. The literal reference-pole exclusion handles the remainder. Hence nu(D^an)=0. Every proper algebraic closed subset lies in an actual divisor: twist its ideal by a sufficiently high ample power and take a nonzero section. Thus every such target is algebraically null. Finite intrinsic dual energy sup[E(u)+int(R-u)dnu] directly implies the required all-test integrability and the same conclusion.

This checks the Root197 proposal's actual tensor powers, all original weights, rank, normalization and genuine closure after reconstructing the scalar foundations; that proposal was not a premise. No absolute integrability of R is assumed. The result does not represent all nonalgebraic polar or negligible sets, establish varying-test continuity against nu, attain an inverse equation or prove comparison and uniqueness.

The precise additional zero-volume theorem is for actual numerically trivial rational bundles, including nontorsion Pic0 bundles, in the varying-actual-bundle numerical cone. The reference is zero. L+epsilon A is actual ample for rational epsilon>0; its generated zero-weight scalar is identically zero, giving a genuine constant defining net. Conversely normalized u in PSH(0) has m u in PSH(0) by tensoring for every positive integer m. All these functions embed into one actual ample cone. Positive ample perturbations have raw mass epsilon^n A^n tending to zero; every continuous integral is bounded by this mass times the test norm. Their operator limit is zero and their constant energies tend to zero. Thus E1(0)=R, raw energy and operator are zero, the only positive mass-zero target is zero, and there is one solution class modulo constants. Comparison and both derivatives are trivial. No division by zero occurs.

Perturbing by epsilon O(1,1) gives positive top masses 2epsilon(1+epsilon) tending to zero for both. Their raw zero equations agree although their difference is not constant.
